issues.failure_explanation: The preceding inequality \sqrt{(a^2-b^2-1)^2+4a^2b^2}+(a^2-b^2-1)>2(a^2-1) simplifies to \sqrt{(a^2-b^2-1)^2+4a^2b^2}>a^2+b^2-1. Using the identity (a^2-b^2-1)^2+4a^2b^2=(a^2+b^2-1)^2+4b^2, the correct simplified form is \sqrt{(a^2+b^2-1)^2+4b^2}>a^2+b^2-1. The proof instead writes (a^2+b^2-1)^2+4a^2b^2 (replacing 4b^2 with 4a^2b^2), which is a different, non-equivalent expression. The conclusion of the theorem is nonetheless correct because the correct inequality reduces to 4b^2>0 (true for b≠0).

failure_location.quote:
This inequality simplifies to 
$$
\sqrt{(a^2 + b^2 - 1)^2 + 4a^2b^2} > a^2 + b^2 - 1,
$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the incorrect simplification with the correct identity (a^2-b^2-1)^2+4a^2b^2=(a^2+b^2-1)^2+4b^2, noting that the resulting inequality holds since 4b^2>0 for b≠0.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:convergence has a gap from an incorrect algebraic simplification. The theorem's conclusion ρ(λ_j)<σ_j remains correct and all downstream uses (e.g., Algorithm alg:AssignIterations) are unaffected.
issues.title: Algebraic error in proof of complex-shift convergence bound
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction of one proof step preserves the theorem statement and all downstream claims; no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\Re(\xi_j^{(1)})\ne\Re(\xi_j^{(N)}) $ it is straightforward to show that $\frac{| \xi_j^{(1)}-\xi_j^{(N)}| }{ |\xi_j^{(1)}| + | \xi_j^{(N)}|  } < \frac{|\xi_j^{(1)}-\xi_j^{(N)}|}{|\xi_j^{(1)}+\xi_j^{(N)}|}$

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed strict inequality requires strict triangle inequality |ξ_j^(1)|+|ξ_j^(N)|>|ξ_j^(1)+ξ_j^(N)|, which holds iff ξ_j^(1) and ξ_j^(N) are not non-negative real multiples of each other. For real λ_j (j'∈{1,ℓ/2+1}) both eigenvalues are positive reals on the same ray, so the triangle inequality is an equality and the strict claim fails. The proof's stated condition Re(ξ_j^(1))≠Re(ξ_j^(N)) (i.e., μ₁≠μ_N) does not imply strictness; the correct condition is Im(λ_j)≠0. The displayed non-strict inequality (≤) is correct for all λ_j.

failure_location.quote: For $p=1$ the maximal value of the optimal polynomial $\poly_1^{\ast}$ is strictly smaller than the maximum value of the scaled Chebyshev polynomial

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the proposition to complex λ_j (e.g., j∈{2,…,ℓ/2}∪{ℓ/2+2,…,ℓ}) and use Im(λ_j)≠0 in the proof to establish strict triangle inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's strict inequality is false for real shifts λ_j. The non-strict inequality in the display remains valid. Downstream claims (Chebyshev polynomials are non-optimal for complex shifts) concern only complex λ_j and are unaffected.
issues.title: Strict inequality in optimal-polynomial claim is false for real shifts
issues.why_classification: Adding a hypothesis restriction and correcting the proof justification is a local fix; the non-strict inequality and all downstream claims for complex shifts survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Separating (A−λ_j I)x_j=b_j into real and imaginary parts with x_j=Re(x_j)+i·Im(x_j) and b_j=Re(b_j)+i·Im(b_j) yields, after substituting v=−Im(x_j) and swapping block rows to obtain the saddle point matrix 𝒮, the right-hand side (−Im(b_j), Re(b_j))^T. The paper writes (−Re(b_j), Im(b_j))^T, interchanging Re(b_j) and Im(b_j). Thus the saddle point system as stated does not solve the original complex system and would produce a wrong solution vector for any b_j with Re(b_j)≠Im(b_j).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap Re(b_j) and Im(b_j) in the right-hand side of Eq. (eq:saddlesystem), changing it to (−Im(b_j), Re(b_j))^T.
issues.overall_effect: The saddle point reformulation of Eq. (eq:blockproblem) as written solves a different complex system (with Re(b_j) and Im(b_j) interchanged). The matrix 𝒮 and the eigenvalue analysis of Theorem thm:added-2 are about the correct matrix and are unaffected.
issues.title: Saddle point system right-hand side swaps Re(b_j) and Im(b_j)
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local swap of two terms in one displayed equation; the matrix 𝒮, all spectral theory, and the method definition survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This has the form of $S_2^{-1}S$ in \cite[Theorem 4]{pearson2012new}, with $\psimat = \frac{1}{\beta}M$, $\phimat = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\beta}}K$ ($M$ and $K$ denoting finite element mass and stiffness matrices, which could be replaced with alternative discretizations of the identity and negative Laplacian operators), and $\beta = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Φ = Im(λ_j)I_N is claimed to be symmetric positive definite but is negative definite whenever Im(λ_j)<0 (which occurs for j∈{ℓ/2+2,…,ℓ}). The proof invokes [pearson2012new, Theorem 4], which requires Φ and Ψ to be SPD; outside this hypothesis the bound ζ²∈[1/2,1] is false. For example with Φ=−0.8I and Ψ=2.5I one computes ζ²≈2.385, outside [1/2,1]. Furthermore Φ+Ψ=A+(Im(λ_j)−Re(λ_j))I can be indefinite (e.g., μ_N≈1.05, λ_j=0.309−0.951i gives minimum eigenvalue ≈−0.21), making 𝒫_D indefinite and removing the MINRES SPD-preconditioner guarantee.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of the preconditioned system $\mathcal{P}_{D}^{-1}\mathcal{S}$ lie in  $\big[-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big] \cup \big[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},1\big]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the saddle point analysis and Theorem thm:added-2 to Im(λ_j)>0, and handle Im(λ_j)<0 shifts by solving for the conjugate shift λ̄_j (which has Im(λ̄_j)>0) and conjugating the solution, using the complex-conjugate pair structure already identified in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: For all complex shifts with Im(λ_j)<0 (half of the complex sub-problems), the eigenvalue bounds of Theorem thm:added-2 are false, Φ is not SPD, and 𝒫_D may be indefinite, so MINRES convergence is not guaranteed. The approach 𝒫_SP lacks a theoretical basis for these sub-problems.
issues.title: Saddle point eigenvalue bounds fail for shifts with negative imaginary part
issues.why_classification: The conjugate-shift workaround is a standard contained argument that preserves the method, scope, rate, and all guarantees; no new lemma, construction, or replacement proof architecture is required.
